summary: Complete attack on all 97 items against the full 49-page published paper: five findings (four high, one medium). Correct the dyadic block-rank exponent, restore a finite Laurent term, repair two counting-proof slips, guard the Gamma/Pochhammer library identity, and restrict Hodge index to numerical divisor classes. None is a counterexample to the main Picard-rank-jump theorem.

Read the complete published paper, pp.1–49, and all 97 extraction items, the complete reader, accepted review, 9 routes, 24 prerequisite records and all existing E1–E6. Inventory: 89 missing, 4 planned, 4 library. Each of the 89 missing items occurs in exactly one route. Current Protocol §16 assigns supplier proof closure and detailed APIs/tests to the consuming blueprint; their absence is not an extraction defect.

Checked the positive-represented-m, maximal-lattice, signature, weak Hodge-genericity, good-reduction and square-class hypotheses, all-prime integral-model interfaces, local and archimedean estimates, thin exceptional set, successive-minima argument, local intersection lattice filtration, global contradiction and K3/abelian/unitary applications. The six existing sourceIssues remain existing diagnostics, including the odd-b square-class repair and the illustrative §7.3 approximation-growth correction; they are not counted again.

Read all 15 explicitly cited library declarations at the actual pinned commits. Tau Ceti: IntegralLattice, dualCarrier, DiscriminantGroup, IsEven, signature, evenIntermediateCarrierOrderIsoIsotropicSubgroup and IntermediateCarrier.isEven_iff_isIsotropic_discriminantSubgroup. Mathlib: CliffordAlgebra, evenOdd, gradedAlgebra, even, ordinaryHypergeometric, ordinaryHypergeometricSeries, ascPochhammer and Complex.Gamma. Additionally read Complex.Gamma_zero, Gamma_neg_nat_eq_zero and Gamma_add_nat_div_Gamma_eq to test the parameter boundary. The paper’s Q equals half the integral bilinear norm, as the extraction notes.

Read the reviewed library-coverage entries and owner statements for PEL M1/M5, abelian schemes A4, Néron R11.1, SF.5, GN.1/GN.3/GN.4, ES.3/ES.4, QM.3, R28.4 and AN.2. Reassembled 2,907 stages and 8,322 stage edges. Read the relevant Shimura V0/V5/V6, datum D5 and GZ.6/GZ.7 boundaries. The orthogonal and K3 candidate IDs reuse the Charles-16 proposals; no draft roadmap defining either was found. Their all-prime arithmetic additions exceed the generic-fibre Shimura and curve-height scopes. Generic quadratic densities remain GN.3 work and circle-method counts ES work; do not privately rebuild their common density normalization.

Pinned whole-tree name searches for Kuga–Satake, Borcherds, Grothendieck–Messing, Hodge index, Minkowski’s second theorem, Maass and Mertens found no corresponding implementation. Mathlib matches were unrelated Borcherds/author-name occurrences. This is bounded corroboration of the reviewed audits, not a universal nonexistence proof.

Reproduced the dyadic example by exhaustive finite enumeration for n=1,2; derived the finite-part product rule algebraically and evaluated its coefficient at b=4; checked the missing-shell count by the rank/discreteness argument and the Hodge-index overgeneralization on E×P¹. These are mathematical counterchecks, not Lean elaborations.

Correction search dated 2026-10-01: published Cambridge PDF and indexed article record, arXiv 1909.07473 submission history (latest v3, 29 August 2022), Yunqing Tang’s Berkeley and Salim Tayou’s Dartmouth publication pages, Crossref DOI 10.1017/fmp.2022.14 (empty relation and no update record), and title/author erratum/correction searches. No correction of the newly reported passages was located. The Cambridge HTML open failed, but the full published PDF was acquired. This does not establish that no correction exists elsewhere.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22.result.json: items /40–/41, sourceIssues, GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.3 route; corresponding reader passages
findings.claim: The extracted dyadic reduction formula is false because s_i counts Jordan blocks rather than their total rank. Rank-two blocks occur at 2; the odd-prime formulas do not expose the error.
findings.evidence: Published p.16 defines s_i as the “size of S_i” and Lemma 4.2(2) uses p^(r−s_0) for the bad-to-good multiplicity. Items /40 and /41 repeat both. Hanke 2004, printed p.360, instead defines s_i=Σ_{j∈S_i} dim(Q_j). Take Q(a,b,c,d,t)=ab+cd+2t², L=U⊕U⊕⟨4⟩, rank r=5 and signature (3,2). This is maximal: its discriminant quadratic module is Z/4 with q(j)=j²/8 mod Z, whose only isotropic element is zero. At 2 there are two rank-two blocks of exponent 0 and one unary block of exponent 1, so the printed s_0 is 2 whereas the rank sum is 4. For m=2, n=1, bad solutions modulo 4 have a,b,c,d even and t odd: exactly 32. Q′=2ab+2cd+t² has 16 good norm-1 solutions modulo 2. The printed formula predicts 2^(5−2)·16=128; the corrected formula gives 2^(5−4)·16=32. Exhaustive enumeration also gives 640 versus 320 at n=2 (printed prediction 2560, corrected 640). The published page image confirms the definition and exponent; E1–E6 do not register it.
findings.fix: Replace s_i=#S_i by s_i=Σ_{j:ν_j=i} rank(L_j) in /40 and carry that convention through /41 and every dyadic consumer and route brief. Preserve the formulas after this replacement; for odd p the two conventions coincide. Add a sourceIssues error at p.16, affecting Lemma 4.2 as stated, with Hanke p.360 as the correct original source. Include the U⊕U⊕⟨4⟩ counts as a regression example. This does not refute the main Picard-jump theorem.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22.result.json: item /66, sourceIssues, GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights route; corresponding reader passages
findings.claim: The exact regularized Green-function decomposition drops a nonzero finite Laurent term when it replaces a holomorphic Gamma factor by its value at the pole. Its limit alone does not justify the equality in (5.8)–(5.9).
findings.evidence: Published p.24 (5.3), p.25 (5.4) and p.28 (5.8)–(5.9), also item /66. Put k=1+b/2 and A(s)=2Γ(k−1+s)/Γ(k+2s). Write the series in (5.3) at parameter k/2+s as S(s), so φ_m(x,k/2+s)=A(s)S(s), A(0)=4/b and Res_{s=0}(AS)=−c(m). The printed tildeφ_m(x,0)+R_x(0,m) is FP(A(0)S), whereas φ_m(x)=FP(AS). Their difference is A′(0)Res(S)=−c(m)[ψ(k−1)−2ψ(k)], with ψ=Γ′/Γ. For b=4 this is c(m)(2−γ), nonzero for represented m. A compatible maximal example is U²⊕A₂, and m=1 is represented. The page images verify all factors and the residue sign. None of E1–E6 treats this regularization correction.
findings.fix: Keep the definitions of tildeφ and R, and replace the exact identity by φ_m(x)=tildeφ_m(x,0)+R_x(0,m)−c(m)[ψ(k−1)−2ψ(k)]. Alternatively absorb this explicit scalar into a newly distinguished corrected R, updating every identity about R consistently. Add a sourceIssues error against (5.8)–(5.9), affecting that exact identity. Explain that the scalar is O(|c(m)|)=O(m^(b/2)), so Proposition 5.4 and the stated downstream asymptotic orders survive; do not withdraw the main theorem. Use the finite-part product rule as the regression check.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22.result.json: items /56 and /68, sourceIssues, GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights brief; corresponding reader passages
findings.claim: Two printed lattice-counting proof slips remain unregistered. Item /68 repeats a count without its norm-shell constraint, making that count infinite; the source weight construction for /56 has the wrong sign on the negative plane and insufficient positive-plane support.
findings.evidence: Published p.31, first display, and /68 omit Q(λ)=1 from #{√mλ∈L: |Q(λ_x)|≤1}; all neighboring sums retain it. For any rank-(b+2) lattice with b≥3 this unconstrained strip contains infinitely many lattice points. Projection to the two-dimensional negative plane either has a nonzero lattice kernel (use its multiples), or has a nondiscrete rank-(b+2) image, hence infinitely many points near zero. Corollary 4.12 bounds only the norm shell. Published p.22, proof of Corollary 4.12, requires ω_P≥1 for Q(λ_x)<T although Q is negative definite on P: this demands ω_P≥1 everywhere and cannot give the claimed compact support. Also, on Q(λ)=1 with −Q(λ_x)≤T≤1, Q(λ_{x⊥})=1−Q(λ_x) ranges up to 2, but the printed positive-plane cutoff is only ≥1 up to 1 and vanishes at 2. Images at pp.22 and 31 confirm these slips; existing E4–E5 cover other errors, not these.
findings.fix: Restore Q(λ)=1 in /68 and the reader count. For /56 retain the correct theorem and supply cutoffs with ω_P≥1 on −Q≤T, vanishing for −Q≥2T, and ω_{P⊥}≥1 on Q≤2, vanishing for Q≥3. Smooth nonnegative bounded cutoffs then majorize the required shell; the singular integral is still O(T). Add separate sourceIssues misprints for the omitted shell and the cutoff signs/radii, affects:the proof, and link their corrected forms to /56 and /68. Preserve the theorem conclusions.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22.result.json: item /4 and sourceIssues; corresponding reader passages
findings.claim: The unguarded Gamma quotient for the Pochhammer symbol is not the cited pinned-library identity. At nonpositive integral parameters Mathlib totalizes Gamma to zero, whereas ascPochhammer is a polynomial.
findings.evidence: Item /4 writes (a)_n=Γ(a+n)/Γ(a) without a parameter restriction; published p.24 introduces this for complex parameters. At Mathlib 082e2d3, RingTheory/Polynomial/Pochhammer.lean:51–60 defines ascPochhammer 0=1 and ascPochhammer 1=X. Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Basic.lean:340–344 proves Complex.Gamma_zero and Gamma_neg_nat_eq_zero. Thus a=0,n=0 gives 1 on the polynomial side but 0/0=0 on the totalized quotient side. The actual theorem Complex.Gamma_add_nat_div_Gamma_eq, Gamma/Beta.lean:460–461, explicitly assumes ∀k:ℕ, a≠−k. OrdinaryHypergeometric.lean:66–82 uses polynomial coefficients, with totalized division; existence of these definitions does not remove the analytic parameter guards.
findings.fix: Define (a)_n by ascPochhammer for all a; state the Gamma-quotient equality only for a outside the nonpositive integers (or explicitly as meromorphic continuation with removable values restored). For the classical analytic series distinguish c outside the nonpositive integers from Mathlib’s totalized definition. Cite the guarded pinned theorem and show that the parameters actually used near k/2 satisfy the guards. Retain status:library for the correctly scoped primitives and add the p.24 source-domain diagnostic. Test a=0,n=0 and a=−1,n=1; these concern the general interface, not failure of the paper’s positive-real-part application.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22.result.json: item /93 and its SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5 interface; corresponding reader passages
findings.claim: The extraction generalizes the K3 application of Hodge index to the full Picard group of every smooth projective surface. For a general surface the nondegenerate form is on real numerical divisor classes, not on its full Picard group.
findings.evidence: Item /93 states the signature (1,ρ−1) on Pic for a smooth projective surface. Published p.44 applies this only to a K3 surface, where the first Chern map is a primitive embedding. Counterexample to the extracted generalization: over C take X=E×P¹ with E an elliptic curve and choose a nontorsion M∈Pic⁰(E). The nontrivial nontorsion class pr_E^*M has zero first Chern class, hence zero intersection with every divisor, and survives in Pic(X)⊗R. The form there has a nonzero radical and does not have the asserted nondegenerate signature. SF.5 is the correct Hodge-index owner; this is a statement-domain error, not a reason to create another roadmap.
findings.fix: State the general theorem on N¹(X)_R (or NS(X)⊗R with the standard identification) and describe the radical when starting from Pic(X)⊗R. Then specialize to the K3 setting using Pic⁰=0 and the primitive first-Chern embedding already in /92. Keep planned:SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5. Record this as an extraction correction, not as an error in the published K3 argument; add E×P¹ with a nontorsion degree-zero line bundle as a domain test.

limitations: Complete means the requested independent attack is finished. It does not certify the entire mathematics or transitive prerequisites. Only the stated Hanke supplier passage was read in addition to the full main paper; the AGHMP, Bruinier–Kühn, André, van Geemen and other supplier proofs were not independently completed.

The exact Gamma/Pochhammer and Hodge-index interfaces are false as written, but their actual positive-parameter and K3 uses admit the stated restrictions. The corrected Laurent scalar has lower asymptotic order. Severity follows Protocol §17’s rule for false statements, not an assertion that the headline theorem fails.
No Lean deliverable is authorized. No compiler, Lake build/cache operation or language server was started.
